request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Age: 69
Sex: Male
Date of Admission: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient was admitted with severely symptomatic atrial fibrillation (AF) requiring multiple cardioversions. He had a history of an implantable cardiac monitor, left bundle branch block with an ejection fraction of 25%, and a cardiac resynchronization therapy device (CRT-D). The patient underwent uncomplicated pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using radiofrequency (RF) via the SANS FLUORO technique. There were no complications during or after the procedure. The patient was discharged the following day and remained free of AF at his three- and six-month follow-up visits.

HISTORY AND FINDINGS:
The patient had previously undergone successful implantation of the Optimizer™ III device as part of a clinical trial. The preprocedure chest radiograph showed increased scar burden in the left atrium (LA) based on voltage mapping, with ablation lesions showing the left atrial roof and posterior line. Post-PVI, entrance and exit blocks were demonstrated. The postprocedure CRT-D check revealed no change in lead sensing, threshold, or impedance values.
DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
PROCEDURE/TREATMENT:
Uncomplicated pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) using radiofrequency (RF) via the SANS FLUORO technique.

FOLLOW-UP:
The patient remained free of AF at his three- and six-month follow-up visits.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
The patient is instructed to follow up with their healthcare provider as recommended.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
N/A

DISCHARGE CONDITION:
The patient was discharged in stable condition.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The patient was admitted for severely symptomatic atrial fibrillation and underwent pulmonary vein isolation to treat it. That makes atrial fibrillation the condition chiefly responsible for the episode.

- The heart failure (ejection fraction 25%), left bundle branch block and implanted devices are comorbidities, not the reason for admission.
- The ablation is the procedure, not the diagnosis.
- Atrial fibrillation is a circulatory condition, so the chapter letter is I.
- Within that chapter, atrial fibrillation and flutter fall under category I48.

CODE: I48
